title: The support colour ramp is not an ordinal ramp: four hues over 156 deg, lightness out of order, 'probable' 2.50:1 and 'withdrawn' 2.85:1 against white
evidence: Tokens (epistemic.css:32-36): confirmed hsl(214 80% 38%) #1357ae, strong hsl(206 72% 44%) #1f7bc1, probable hsl(41 88% 45%) #d8980e, weak hsl(28 82% 48%) #df7416, unsupported grey. dataviz validate_palette.js --ordinal on weak->confirmed: FAIL lightness monotone (OKLCH L 0.67/0.724/0.566/0.468), FAIL adjacent dL (weak/probable 0.054), FAIL single hue (spread 156 deg). WCAG contrast vs #fff (tools/contrast.py): probable 2.50, weak 3.17, unsupported 3.35, withdrawn (:54, #999999) 2.85 -> probable and withdrawn below the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11) where the chip border is the colour channel. In greyscale/print 'probable' reads as the weakest support. Glyph + text still carry meaning (SIG-UI-005), so severity S3.
